segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: OK, Greg, so I finally managed to read the article you mentioned – the one about the study on gender in physics.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: About the study of college students done by Akira Miyake and his team? Yeah. I was interested that the researchers were actually a mix of psychologists and physicists. That’s an unusual combination.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: Yeah. I got a little confused at first about which students the study was based on. They weren’t actually majoring in physics – they were majoring in what’s known as the STEM disciplines. That’s science, technology, engineering and ... [[ ]]

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: ... and math. Yes, but they were all doing physics courses as part of their studies.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: That’s correct. So as I understood it, Miyake and co started from the fact that women are underrepresented in introductory physics courses at college, and also that on average, the women who do enrol on these courses perform more poorly than the men. No one really knows why this is the case.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Yeah. But what the researchers wanted to find out was basically what they could do about the relatively low level of the women’s results [[ ]] . But in order to find a solution they needed to find out more about the nature of the problem.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: Right – now let’s see if I can remember ... it was that in the physics class, the female students thought the male students all assumed that women weren’t any good at physics ... was that it? And they thought that the men expected them to get poor results in their tests.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: That’s what the women thought, and that made them nervous, so they did get poor results. But actually they were wrong ... No one was making any assumption about the female students at all. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: Anyway, what Miyake’s team did was quite simple – getting the students to do some writing before they went into the physics class. What did they call it?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Values-affirmation – they had to write an essay focusing on things that were significant to them, not particularly to do with the subject they were studying, but more general things like music or people who mattered to them. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: Right. So the idea of doing the writing is that this gets the students thinking in a positive way.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: And putting these thoughts into words can relax them and help them overcome the psychological factors that lead to poor performance [[ ]] . Yeah. But what the researchers in the study hadn’t expected was that this one activity raised the women’s physics grades from the C to the B range. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: A huge change. Pity it wasn’t to an A, but still! No, but it does suggest that the women were seriously underperforming beforehand, in comparison with the men.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Yes. Mind you, Miyake’s article left out a lot of details. Like, did the students to the writing just once, or several times? And had they been told why they were doing the writing? That might have affected the results. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: You mean, if they know the researchers thought it might help them to improve, then they’d just try to fulfil that expectation?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Exactly. ——————-

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: So anyway, I thought for our project we could do a similar study, but investigate whether it really was the writing activity that had that result.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: OK. So we could ask them to do a writing task about something completely different ... something more factual? Like a general knowledge topic.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Maybe ... or we could have half the students doing a writing task and half doing something else, like an oral task.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: Or even, half do the same writing task as in the original research and half do a factual writing task [[ ]] . Then we’d see if it really is the topic that made the difference, or something else.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: That’s it. Good. So at our meeting with the supervisor on Monday we can tell him we’ve decided on our project. We should have our aims ready by then. I suppose we need to read the original study – the article’s just a summary.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: And these was another article I read, by Smolinsky. It was about her research on how women and men perform in mixed teams in class, compared with single-sex teams and on their own.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Let me guess ... the women were better at teamwork.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: That’s what I expected, but actually the men and the women got the same results whether they were working in teams or on their own [[ ]] . But I guess it’s not that relevant to us.

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: What worries me anyway is how we’re going to get everything done in the time.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: We’ll be OK now we know what we’re doing. Though I’m not clear how we assess whether the students in our experiment actually make any progress or not ...

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: No. We may need some advice on that. The main thing’s to make sure we have the right size sample, not too big or too small.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: That shouldn’t be difficult. Right, what do we need to do next? We could have a look at the timetable for the science classes ... or perhaps we should just make an appointment to see one of the science professors. That’d be better. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Great. And we could even get to observe one of the classes.

segments.speaker: LISA
segments.en: What for?

segments.speaker: GREG
segments.en: Well ... OK maybe let’s just go with your idea. Right, well ...

instructions: Complete the original Cambridge IELTS listening questions below.
questions.source_text:
SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
STUDY ON GENDER IN PHYSICS
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: The students in Akira Miyake's study were all majoring in
    Options:
        physics.
        psychology or physics.
        science, technology, engineering or mathematics.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: The aim of Miyake's study was to investigate
    Options:
        what kind of women choose to study physics.
        a way of improving women's performance in physics.
        whether fewer women than men study physics at college.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: The female physics students were wrong to believe that
    Options:
        the teachers marked them in an unfair way.
        the male students expected them to do badly.
        their test results were lower than the male students'.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: Miyake's team asked the students to write about
    Options:
        what they enjoyed about studying physics.
        the successful experiences of other people.
        something that was important to them personally.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: What was the aim of the writing exercise done by the subjects?
    Options:
        to reduce stress.
        to strengthen verbal ability.
        to encourage logical thinking.
    Q Num: 26
    Text: What surprised the researchers about the study?
    Options:
        how few students managed to get A grades.
        the positive impact it had on physics results for women.
        the difference between male and female performance.
    Q Num: 27
    Text: Greg and Lisa think Miyake's results could have been affected by
    Options:
        the length of the writing task.
        the number of students who took part.
        the information the students were given.
    Q Num: 28
    Text: Greg and Lisa decide that in their own project, they will compare the effects of
    Options:
        two different writing tasks.
        a writing task with an oral task.
        two different oral tasks.
    Q Num: 29
    Text: The main finding of Smolinsky's research was that class teamwork activities
    Options:
        were most effective when done by all-women groups.
        had no effect on the performance of men or women.
        improved the results of men more than of women.
    Q Num: 30
    Text: What will Lisa and Greg do next?
    Options:
        talk to a professor.
        observe a science class.
        look at the science timetable.
